items.title: The model vocabulary of stability and chaos: the associated flow of a declared force model, equilibria, periodic and homoclinic orbits, and invariant sets
items.statement:
This item fixes the vocabulary in which the stability, perturbation and chaos
statements of this page are phrased. All objects below are model data; nothing
here is a measured value, and no clause asserts that a particular model has an
equilibrium, a periodic orbit or an invariant set.

**(i) The model class.** A **stability model** is a force model of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N\ge1$ labels, fixed masses
$m_1,\dots,m_N>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), a time window
$I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior, an open configuration domain
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]), and a force map
$F:D\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ on an open set
$D\subseteq I_0\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, continuous and locally Lipschitz
in the state variable, whose **motions** are the $C^2$ curves $x:J\to Q$ of
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]] (that is, $m_ix_i''=F_i(t,x,x')$ on $J$ and
$(t,x(t),x'(t))\in D$). The model is **autonomous** when $I_0=\mathbb R$ and
$D=\mathbb R\times S_0$ for an open **state domain**
$S_0\subseteq Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ with $F(x,v)$ independent of $t$, and
**$P$-periodic** for a period $P>0$ when $I_0=\mathbb R$ and
$F(t+P,x,v)=F(t,x,v)$ for all $(t,x,v)\in D$. All time intervals use the
frame-time parameter fixed by [[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]] with
$[t]=\tau$ ([[def-cm01-units]]).

**(ii) Associated field and flow.** Write $n:=3N$,
$\mathsf M:=\operatorname{diag}(m_1I_3,\dots,m_NI_3)$, and let
$$Z(t,x,v):=\bigl(v,\ \mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)\bigr)$$
be the **associated first-order field** of the model, on the same domain $D$;
the state curve $z:=(x,x')$ of a motion is a solution of $z'=Z(t,z)$ and
conversely ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]] clause (c)). For an autonomous model
write $G:S_0\to\mathbb R^{6N}$, $G(x,v):=(v,\mathsf M^{-1}F(x,v))$; by the
standing regularity of $F$, the field $G$ is continuous and locally Lipschitz
in the state, so it has a **local flow**
$$\Phi:\Omega\longrightarrow S_0,\qquad \Phi(t,z_0):=z(t;z_0),$$
with maximal solutions $z(\,\cdot\,;z_0):I_{z_0}\to S_0$ and flow domain
$\Omega=\{(t,z_0):t\in I_{z_0}\}$, in the sense of
[[def-cm-local-flow-of-an-autonomous-system]]. The model's motions with state
curve through $z_0$ at time $0$ are exactly the curves $t\mapsto\Phi(t,z_0)$
restricted to their maximal intervals, and
$\Phi(s+t,z_0)=\Phi(t,\Phi(s,z_0))$ wherever both sides are defined
([[lem-cm-local-flow-composition-law]]). If in addition $F$ is of class $C^1$
in the state, then $\Omega$ is open and $\Phi$ is $C^1$ on it
([[cor-cm-flow-domain-open-and-flow-is-c1]]). No completeness of $\Phi$ is
asserted: the maximal interval $I_{z_0}$ may be bounded
([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]).

**(iii) Equilibria and periodic orbits.** A state $z_*=(x_*,v_*)\in S_0$ is an
**equilibrium state** of the autonomous model when $G(z_*)=0$, that is
$v_*=0$ and $F(x_*,0)=0$; under that condition the constant curve
$x(t)=x_*$ is a motion. A **periodic orbit** of the model is a motion
$x:\mathbb R\to Q$ that is not constant and satisfies $x(t+T)=x(t)$ for all
$t\in\mathbb R$ and some $T>0$; the infimum of all such $T$ is its **least
period**. A **limit cycle** (also **closed orbit**) is a periodic orbit whose
image is isolated among images of periodic orbits: there is an open set
$U\supseteq x(\mathbb R)$ such that no other periodic orbit has image meeting
$U$. A limit cycle's attraction is a separate property and is not part of this
definition.

**(iv) Invariant sets.** A set $S\subseteq S_0$ is **invariant** for the
autonomous model when $(t,z)\in\Omega$ for every $z\in S$ and every
$t\in\mathbb R$, and $\Phi_t(S)=S$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$, where
$\Phi_t(z):=\Phi(t,z)$; it is **forward invariant** when $(t,z)\in\Omega$ for
every $z\in S$, $t\ge0$, and $\Phi_t(S)\subseteq S$ for every $t\ge0$. The
**orbital distance** from a state $z$ to a nonempty set $S$ is
$$d(z,S):=\inf_{s\in S}\lVert z-s\rVert_2,$$
with the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] on the state
chart.

**(v) Homoclinic and heteroclinic orbits.** A motion with state curve $z$ is
**homoclinic to** an equilibrium state $z_*$ when $z(t)\to z_*$ as
$t\to+\infty$ and as $t\to-\infty$, and is **heteroclinic from $z_-$ to
$z_+$** for distinct equilibrium states $z_-,z_+$ when $z(t)\to z_-$ as
$t\to-\infty$ and $z(t)\to z_+$ as $t\to+\infty$. Both are limit relations
of the model's motions, not intersections of separately constructed geometric
objects; the differentiability of the associated stable and unstable sets is
not asserted here.

**(vi) Reading conventions.** (a) The vocabulary is attached to the declared
model class; equilibria, periodic orbits, invariant sets and homoclinic orbits
are model objects, and no clause asserts that a physical system is exactly a
stability model or realises any of these objects. (b) The state space is
written in the Cartesian chart; a change of chart changes the coordinate
expression of the field, and the numerical values of derivative spectra depend
on the chart unless coordinates are scaled with fixed factors, while the
model's motions, equilibria, periodic orbits, invariant sets and their
asymptotic properties do not change.
items.strategy: A vocabulary item: the model class, its associated field and local flow with maximal solutions, equilibrium states, periodic orbits and limit cycles, invariant sets and orbital distance, and homoclinic and heteroclinic orbits.
items.physical_scope: The model vocabulary of the page's stability, perturbation and chaos statements: the autonomous force models of the framework (open configuration domain, fixed positive masses, a continuous state-locally-Lipschitz force map), their associated first-order fields and local flows with maximal solutions, equilibrium states (vanishing force at rest), periodic orbits and limit cycles, invariant and forward-invariant sets, orbital distance, and homoclinic and heteroclinic orbits as limit relations of motions. All objects are declared model data; the item asserts no measurement, no existence of any particular equilibrium or periodic orbit, and no stability of any of the listed objects.

items.title: Stability vocabulary of the model: Lyapunov, asymptotic and orbital stability, linear stability of equilibria and periodic orbits, and hyperbolicity of equilibria and fixed points
items.statement:
This item attaches stability predicates to the model vocabulary of
[[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]]. Throughout, an autonomous
stability model is fixed with state domain $S_0$, field $G$, local flow
$\Phi:\Omega\to S_0$ and maximal solutions $z(\,\cdot\,;z_0)$
([[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clauses (i)-(ii)); all
predicates are applied to model objects and quantify over the model's maximal
solutions.

**(i) Lyapunov and asymptotic stability.** Let $z_*\in S_0$ be an equilibrium
state. The state $z_*$ is **Lyapunov stable** when for every Euclidean ball
$B_\varepsilon(z_*)$ with $\overline{B_\varepsilon(z_*)}\subseteq S_0$
([[def-metric-ball]]) there is $\delta\in(0,\varepsilon]$ such that every
maximal solution $z$ with $\lVert z(0)-z_*\rVert_2<\delta$ is defined for all
$t\ge0$ and satisfies $\lVert z(t)-z_*\rVert_2<\varepsilon$ for all $t\ge0$.
It is **asymptotically stable** when it is Lyapunov stable and there is
$\delta_0>0$ such that every maximal solution with
$\lVert z(0)-z_*\rVert_2<\delta_0$ is defined for all $t\ge0$ and converges to
$z_*$ as $t\to\infty$. This is the definition of
[[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]] clauses 1-2, applied to the
autonomous field $G$ on $S_0$; it is recorded here to fix the exact
quantifier order and the requirement that the solutions are defined for all
$t\ge0$. A state that is not Lyapunov stable is **unstable**.

**(ii) Orbital stability of an invariant set.** Let $S\subseteq S_0$ be a
nonempty compact invariant set ([[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]]
clause (iv)). Then $S$ is **orbitally stable** when for every open set
$U\supseteq S$ there is an open set $V$ with $S\subseteq V\subseteq U$ such
that every maximal solution $z$ with $z(0)\in V$ is defined for all $t\ge0$
and satisfies $z(t)\in U$ for all $t\ge0$. The distance used implicitly is
the orbital distance $d(z,S)$ of clause (iv) of the cited definition. Orbital
stability is a statement about the set, not about one motion, and it does not
assert attraction.

**(iii) Linear stability of an equilibrium.** Suppose $F$ is of class $C^1$
in the state, so that $\Phi$ is $C^1$ ([[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]]
clause (ii)) and $DG(z_*)$ exists. The equilibrium $z_*$ is **linearly
stable** when for every $u\in\mathbb R^{6N}$ the maximal solution
$Y:\mathbb R\supseteq J\to M_{6N}(\mathbb R)$ of the variational equation
$$Y'(t)=DG(z_*)Y(t),\qquad Y(0)=u$$
([[def-variational-equation-along-an-ode-solution]], with the constant
solution $z(t)=z_*$ as the reference motion) is defined for all $t\ge0$ and
$\sup_{t\ge0}\lVert Y(t)\rVert_2<\infty$. Linear stability is a statement
about the linear variational equation; it is neither necessary nor sufficient
for Lyapunov stability in general, and no implication between the two is
asserted here. If the variational equation has a solution with
$\lVert Y(t)\rVert_2$ unbounded as $t\to\infty$, the equilibrium is **linearly
unstable**.

**(iv) Hyperbolicity of an equilibrium.** Let $z_*$ be an equilibrium state
of an autonomous model whose force map is $C^1$ in the state, and let
$DG(z_*)$ be the derivative of the associated field at $z_*$. Then $z_*$ is
**hyperbolic** when no complex eigenvalue of $DG(z_*)$
([[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]) has real part $0$;
the eigenvalues are those of the matrix of $DG(z_*)$ in the state chart. The
harmonic oscillator equilibrium of a one-dimensional model with a positive
stiffness has the purely imaginary eigenvalues $\pm i\omega$ and is therefore
not hyperbolic; the saddle of a repulsive linear model has the real
eigenvalues $\pm\mu$, $\mu>0$, and is hyperbolic.

**(v) Linear stability and hyperbolicity of a map.** Let $X\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
be open and let $\Psi:X\to X$ be of class $C^1$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). A **fixed point** of $\Psi$
is a point $a\in X$ with $\Psi(a)=a$. The fixed point is **linearly stable**
when $\sup_{n\ge0}\lVert D\Psi(a)^nu\rVert_2<\infty$ for every
$u\in\mathbb R^m$, and **hyperbolic** when no complex eigenvalue of
$D\Psi(a)$ has modulus $1$. They concern the derivative of the map, not
the nonlinear map.

**(vi) Distinctions.** (a) The five predicates of clauses (i)-(v) are
distinct: a Lyapunov stable equilibrium need not attract; a linearly stable
equilibrium need not be Lyapunov stable and conversely; orbital stability of a
set neither implies nor is implied by stability of any one of its points; a
hyperbolic equilibrium is never linearly stable in the sense of clause (iii)
because the dichotomy of
[[thm-cm-exponential-dichotomy-for-a-hyperbolic-endomorphism]] produces an
exponentially growing solution, but hyperbolicity is not required for
instability. (b) The eigenvalues of $DG(z_*)$ are chart-dependent: they are
unchanged by a linear change of state coordinates with fixed scale factors,
but not by a general chart transition
([[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clause (vi)(b)). (c) For the
mechanical chart data $(M,U)$ of
[[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]], at a mechanical
equilibrium $(q_0,0)$ the derivative of the field is
$DG(q_0,0)(\delta q,\delta v)=(\delta v,-M(q_0)^{-1}D^2U(q_0)\delta q)$; the
stability consequences of that computation are proved later on the page.
items.strategy: A vocabulary item: Lyapunov and asymptotic stability with exact quantifiers, orbital stability of a compact invariant set, linear stability of equilibria and of map fixed points, and hyperbolicity of equilibria and fixed points, with the chart and distinction caveats.
items.physical_scope: The stability predicates attached to the model vocabulary of the page: Lyapunov stability and asymptotic stability of an equilibrium state with their exact quantifiers over maximal solutions, orbital stability of a compact invariant set, linear stability of an equilibrium through bounded solutions of the variational equation, linear stability of a periodic orbit through bounded iterates of the derivative of a return map, and hyperbolicity of an equilibrium of the model's field and of a fixed point of a C1 map (spectra off the imaginary axis or the unit circle). The item records the distinctions between these notions and asserts no stability, instability or attraction of any particular model.

items.title: Energy stability and instability of the mechanical model at an equilibrium: the strict minimum is Lyapunov stable, a negative Hessian eigenvalue gives linear instability, a strictly concave potential gives nonlinear instability, and exact energy conservation rules out attraction
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let
$M:\Omega\to M_n(\mathbb R)$ be a $C^2$ field of symmetric positive definite
matrices, and let $U:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^2$; let $G$ be the
mechanical vector field and $E(q,v)=\tfrac12v^{\mathsf T}M(q)v+U(q)$ the
energy of [[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]]. Let
$q_0\in\Omega$ be a mechanical equilibrium, $\nabla U(q_0)=0$, and put
$K:=D^2U(q_0)$ ([[def-hessian-and-euclidean-critical-point]],
[[cor-hessian-is-symmetric]]). Then:

1. **(Strict minimum.)** If $q_0$ is a strict local minimum of $U$, then
   $(q_0,0)$ is a Lyapunov stable equilibrium of $G$
   ([[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]],
   [[def-cm16-stability-and-hyperbolicity-concepts]] clause (i)).
2. **(Linear instability from a negative eigenvalue.)** If $K$ has a negative
   eigenvalue ([[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]), then
   there are $\mu>0$ and $w\ne0$ in $\mathbb R^n$ such that
   $t\mapsto e^{\mu t}(w,\mu w)$ is a solution of the variational equation
   $Y'=DG(q_0,0)Y$ along the constant solution $z\equiv(q_0,0)$
   ([[def-variational-equation-along-an-ode-solution]]); in particular
   $(q_0,0)$ is linearly unstable in the sense of
   [[def-cm16-stability-and-hyperbolicity-concepts]] clause (iii).
3. **(Nonlinear instability from a strictly concave potential.)** If $K$ is
   negative definite, then every complex eigenvalue of $DG(q_0,0)$ is real
   and nonzero, at least one is positive, and $(q_0,0)$ is unstable: it is
   not Lyapunov stable.
4. **(No attraction under exact energy conservation.)** The energy $E$ is
   constant along every maximal solution of $G$. If there are states
   $z=(q,v)$ with $\lVert z-(q_0,0)\rVert_2$ arbitrarily small and
   $E(z)\ne E(q_0,0)$, then $(q_0,0)$ is not asymptotically stable. In
   particular, if $q_0$ is a strict local minimum of $U$, then $(q_0,0)$ is
   Lyapunov stable but not asymptotically stable.
5. **(Scope.)** No statement is made about a degenerate Hessian $K$ (some
   eigenvalue $0$), and clause 2 gives no nonlinear conclusion when $K$ has
   both a negative and a positive eigenvalue: the linearisation then also has
   purely imaginary eigenvalues and is not hyperbolic, so the instability
   theorem used in clause 3 does not apply. No global stability, no basin of
   attraction and no statement about the size of any neighbourhood is
   claimed.
items.strategy: Direct deduction from the energy-stability, linearisation, quadratic-form and instability suppliers: strict minimum gives Lyapunov stability; negative Hessian eigenvalue gives linear instability; negative definite Hessian gives nonlinear instability; exact energy conservation rules out attraction.
items.physical_scope: The stability consequences of the mechanical chart data at a mechanical equilibrium q0: a strict local minimum of the potential gives a Lyapunov stable equilibrium; a negative Hessian eigenvalue gives an unbounded solution of the linearised variational equation (linear instability, with no nonlinear conclusion); a negative definite Hessian (strict local maximum) makes the equilibrium unstable in the nonlinear sense through the hyperbolic instability theorem; and exact energy conservation along the model's motions prevents asymptotic stability whenever states of different energy accumulate at the equilibrium, so a strict minimum is stable but not attracting. No global stability, no asymptotic stability and no statement about degenerate (zero-eigenvalue) Hessians is claimed.

Konstantin Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), §§3.2 and 5.6: equilibrium types and the warning that precise Lyapunov, asymptotic and linear notions are distinct

items.title: Linearisation along a motion of the mechanical model: the flow derivative solves the variational equation, with Lipschitz dependence, the constant-metric second-order form, and the conditional finite-time error bound of the linear approximation
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let
$M:\Omega\to M_n(\mathbb R)$ be a $C^2$ field of symmetric positive definite
matrices, let $U:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^2$, and let $G$ be the
mechanical vector field on the state domain $S_0:=\Omega\times\mathbb R^n$
([[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]]), so that the
motions of the model are exactly the curves $t\mapsto\Phi(t,z_0)$ of the local
flow of the autonomous field $G$
([[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clause (ii),
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]). Fix a state $z_0=(q_0,v_0)\in S_0$, a time
$T>0$ and a radius $R>0$ such that $\overline B(z_0,R)\subseteq S_0$, put
$$M_R:=\sup_{\overline B(z_0,R)}\lVert G\rVert_2,\qquad L_R:=\sup_{\overline B(z_0,R)}\lVert DG\rVert,$$
and let $0<\rho<R-M_RT$ ([[def-metric-ball]],
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]). Then:

1. **(Flow derivative and variational equation.)** For every $a\in\overline
   B(z_0,\rho)$ the maximal solution $z(\,\cdot\,;a)$ is defined on $[0,T]$
   and stays in $B(z_0,R)$; the map $a\mapsto z(t;a)$ is differentiable at
   every $a\in B(z_0,\rho)$ for $t\in[0,T]$, and for every
   $u\in\mathbb R^{6N}$
   $$D_az(t;a)u=Y_a(t)u,$$
   where $Y_a$ is the unique solution of the variational equation along the
   reference motion $z(\,\cdot\,;a)$,
   $$Y'(t)=DG\bigl(z(t;a)\bigr)Y(t),\qquad Y(0)=I_{6N},$$
   in the sense of [[def-variational-equation-along-an-ode-solution]];
   moreover $\lVert z(t;a)-z(t;b)\rVert_2\le e^{L_Rt}\lVert a-b\rVert_2$ for
   all $a,b\in\overline B(z_0,\rho)$ and $t\in[0,T]$.
2. **(Constant-metric second-order form.)** Suppose in addition that $M$ is
   constant on $\Omega$, say $M(q)\equiv M$ with $M$ symmetric positive
   definite. Then along a motion $q:[0,T]\to\Omega$ with state curve
   $z(t)=(q(t),q'(t))$ the variational equation of clause 1 for a deviation
   $\eta:=Y_q$ (the first $n$ components of $Y$) is equivalent to the
   second-order equation
   $$M\,\eta''(t)=-D^2U\bigl(q(t)\bigr)\eta(t)\qquad(0\le t\le T),$$
   with $D^2U$ the Hessian of $U$
   ([[def-hessian-and-euclidean-critical-point]]).
3. **(Conditional finite-time error bound.)** Suppose in addition that
   $z_0$ is an equilibrium, $G(z_0)=0$, and write $A:=DG(z_0)$; suppose there
   are constants $C\ge0$, $L\ge0$ and $r>0$ with
   $\overline B(z_0,r)\subseteq S_0$ and
   $$\lVert G(z)-A(z-z_0)\rVert_2\le C\lVert z-z_0\rVert_2^2,\qquad \lVert G(z)\rVert_2\le L\lVert z-z_0\rVert_2\qquad(\lVert z-z_0\rVert_2\le r).$$
   Let $T>0$ and $\delta:=\lVert a-z_0\rVert_2>0$ with $\delta e^{LT}<r$, let
   $z(\,\cdot\,;a)$ be the model's motion through $a$, and let $y$ solve the
   linearised equation $y'=Ay$, $y(0)=a-z_0$. Then
   $$\lVert z(t;a)-z_0-y(t)\rVert_2\le C\delta^2\int_0^t e^{\lVert A\rVert(t-s)}e^{2Ls}\,\mathrm ds \le C\delta^2\,t\,e^{(\lVert A\rVert+2L)t}\qquad(0\le t\le T).$$
   under the supplier's interval, where $\lVert A\rVert$ is the operator norm
   ([[def-operator-norm]]).
4. **(Scope.)** The linearised equation approximates the model's motion only
   for finite times and initial states inside the declared ball with the
   declared quantitative bounds; the constants $M_R,L_R,C,L,r$ are model-data
   bounds, not measured quantities. Clause 1 gives no rate of separation
   beyond the exponential bound, no conclusion when the reference motion
   leaves $B(z_0,R)$ before time $T$, and no statement about the size of the
   time interval on which a linearisation is a good approximation; clause 3's
   hypotheses must be verified for the particular data.
items.strategy: Direct transfer of the smooth-dependence and finite-time linearisation suppliers to the mechanical chart model, with the constant-metric second-order form and the conditional quadratic-remainder bound.
items.physical_scope: The linearisation of the mechanical chart model along a declared motion: the derivative of the model's local flow with respect to the initial state solves the variational equation along the motion; nearby initial states separate at most exponentially with the Lipschitz constant of the field; for a constant kinetic metric the second-order linearisation is M eta'' = -D^2 U(x(t)) eta; and whenever the quantitative quadratic remainder and linear growth bounds are declared on a ball, the finite-time difference between the nonlinear motion and the solution of the linearised equation obeys the supplier's explicit bound. The constants C and L are declared model-data bounds; no measured value, no long-time approximation and no global statement is asserted.

items.title: Finite-time tangent growth rates and Lyapunov exponents of the model's flow: the rate per unit time of a transported deviation, with its existence convention and its limits
items.statement:
Let an autonomous stability model be fixed with force map of class $C^1$ in the
state ([[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clauses (i)-(ii)), so
that the associated field $G$ is $C^1$ on the state domain $S_0$ and its local
flow $\Phi:\Omega\to S_0$ is $C^1$ on the open flow domain $\Omega$
([[cor-cm-flow-domain-open-and-flow-is-c1]],
[[def-cm16-stability-and-hyperbolicity-concepts]] clause (iii)).

**(i) The finite-time rate.** Let $z\in S_0$, let $t>0$ with $(t,z)\in\Omega$,
and let $u\in\mathbb R^{6N}\setminus\{0\}$ satisfy
$D_z\Phi_t(z)u\ne0$, where $\Phi_t:=\Phi(t,\cdot)$ and $D_z\Phi_t(z)$ is its
total derivative ([[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clause (ii),
[[def-cm16-stability-and-hyperbolicity-concepts]] clause (iii)). The
**finite-time tangent growth rate of $(z,u)$ over the time $t$** is
$$r(t,z,u):=\frac1t\log\!\left(\frac{\lVert D_z\Phi_t(z)u\rVert_2}{\lVert u\rVert_2}\right)\in\mathbb R,$$
with the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the natural
logarithm of [[def-natural-logarithm]]; this is the definition of
[[def-cm-finite-time-tangent-growth-rate-and-lyapunov-exponent]] applied to
the model's field $G$. The rate has the dimension of inverse time,
$[r]=\tau^{-1}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]): it is a logarithm per unit of the frame
time.

**(ii) The Lyapunov exponent.** If the limit
$$\lambda(z,u):=\lim_{\substack{t\to\infty\\(t,z)\in\Omega}}r(t,z,u)$$
exists in $\mathbb R$, it is the **Lyapunov exponent of $(z,u)$**; if the
limit does not exist, **no exponent is assigned** and no value $+\infty$ or
$-\infty$ is named. In particular the definition does not assert that the
limit exists, and it does not average over an invariant measure or over
initial data.

**(iii) Reading and chart dependence.** (a) A positive rate at time $t$ says
that the deviation $u$ has grown by a factor $e^{r(t,z,u)t}$ in the Euclidean
state norm on $[0,t]$; a negative rate says it has shrunk. (b) The rate
depends on the norm and on the state chart: scaling the state coordinates by
positive constants multiplies distances by a bounded factor and changes
$r(t,z,u)$ by at most $t^{-1}\log(\text{scale ratio})$, so the large-time
exponent is unchanged by fixed rescaling but need not be preserved by an
unbounded chart change
([[def-cm16-stability-and-hyperbolicity-concepts]] clause (vi)(b)). (c) The
rate is attached to a state and a tangent vector and requires the reference
state to remain in the flow domain for the whole time $t$; if the maximal
solution through $z$ is not defined on $[0,t]$, no rate is assigned at
$(z,t)$.

**(iv) What the rate does not assert.** A positive finite-time rate is not a
definition of chaos, not a claim that the model's flow has a chaotic invariant
set, and not an instability statement about the reference motion; it is a
property of the linearised flow over the stated time. In particular, a
hyperbolic equilibrium of the linear models used in the page's checks has
positive rates along its unstable directions while its compact invariant sets
need not be chaotic (see the page's counterexample on the repulsive linear
model). No probabilistic, almost-everywhere or empirical claim is made by this
definition.
items.strategy: A vocabulary item: the finite-time tangent growth rate and the Lyapunov exponent, their dimensions, chart dependence and the exact limits of what a positive rate asserts.
items.physical_scope: The finite-time tangent growth rate and, when the limit exists, the Lyapunov exponent of a declared autonomy model whose force map is of class C1 in the state: the rate is the logarithm per unit time of the Euclidean norm of a nonzero transported deviation vector, and the exponent is assigned only when the limit over the declared time interval exists. The item fixes the definition, its dependence on the chart and norm, and the boundaries of what the rate does and does not assert (positive finite-time growth is not chaos, not instability of a trajectory and not an invariant of a change of coordinates).

items.title: The stroboscopic map of a periodic model and the Poincare return map of a transversal section: domains, iterates, fixed points and the local C1 diffeomorphism property
items.statement:
**(i) The stroboscopic map.** Let a $P$-periodic stability model be fixed
($P>0$; [[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clause (i)) with state
curve $z(t;z_0)=(x(t;z_0),x'(t;z_0))$ of the motion through $z_0$ at time $0$
and maximal interval $I_{z_0}$. The **stroboscopic map at period $P$** is the
partial map
$$\Psi:\Sigma\longrightarrow S_0,\qquad \Sigma:=\{z_0\in S_0:[0,P]\subseteq I_{z_0}\},\qquad \Psi(z_0):=z(P;z_0),$$
with domain $\Sigma$ the set of states whose maximal motion exists over
$[0,P]$. Its **iterates** are defined recursively by $\Psi^1:=\Psi$ and, where
$\Psi^n(z_0)\in\Sigma$, $\Psi^{n+1}(z_0):=\Psi(\Psi^n(z_0))$; the domain of
$\Psi^n$ is therefore the set of states whose maximal motion exists over
$[0,nP]$, and it may be strictly smaller than $\Sigma$. A state
$z_*\in\Sigma$ with $\Psi(z_*)=z_*$ is a **fixed point** of $\Psi$, and it is
a **$P$-periodic state** of the model: the motion through $z_*$ satisfies
$z(t+P;z_*)=z(t;z_*)$ for all $t$ for which both sides are defined. No
completeness of $\Psi$ is asserted: $\Sigma$ need not be all of $S_0$, and
iterates can leave the domain.

**(ii) Autonomous special case.** If the model is autonomous, then its
stroboscopic map at any period $P>0$ is the time-$P$ map $\Phi_P$ of its local
flow restricted to $\Omega_P=\{(P,z):(P,z)\in\Omega\}$
([[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clause (ii)); this is the
reading used for the isotropic-oscillator check on the page.

**(iii) The Poincare return map.** Let an autonomous model with force map of
class $C^1$ in the state be fixed, with associated $C^1$ field $G$ on $S_0$
and local flow $\Phi:\Omega\to S_0$
([[cor-cm-flow-domain-open-and-flow-is-c1]]). Let $z_0\in S_0$, $t_0>0$ with
$(t_0,z_0)\in\Omega$, put $z_1:=\Phi(t_0,z_0)$, let $W\subseteq S_0$ be open
with $z_0,z_1\in W$, and let $h:W\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ with
$h(z_0)=h(z_1)=0$ and $Dh(z_0)G(z_0)\ne0$, $Dh(z_1)G(z_1)\ne0$. The
**section** is $\Sigma_h:=\{z\in W:h(z)=0\}$, and the reference orbit meets it
transversally at $z_0$ and again at $z_1$. Then
[[prop-cm-first-return-map-is-a-local-c1-diffeomorphism]] supplies open sets
$A\ni z_0$, $B\ni z_1$ and $C^1$ functions $\tau:A\to\mathbb R$,
$\sigma:B\to\mathbb R$ with $\tau(z_0)=\sigma(z_1)=t_0$ such that
$$P:A\cap\Sigma_h\longrightarrow\Sigma_h,\qquad P(z):=\Phi\bigl(\tau(z),z\bigr)$$
is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto $P(A\cap\Sigma_h)$, which is open in the
subspace topology of $\Sigma_h$ ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]), with inverse
$Q(z)=\Phi(-\sigma(z),z)$; moreover $h(\Phi(t,z))=0$ for $(t,z)\in J\times A$
holds exactly for $t=\tau(z)$, so $P$ is the **local first-return map** of the
section through the reference orbit. A state $z_*\in A\cap\Sigma_h$ with
$P(z_*)=z_*$ is a **fixed point of the return map**, and the motion through
$z_*$ is periodic with period $\tau(z_*)$.

**(iv) Conventions and scope.** (a) Both maps are attached to the declared
model and its flow; the stroboscopic map depends on the chosen period $P$ and
the return map on the chosen section and reference crossing, and different
choices give different (conjugate only under the stated conditions) maps.
(b) The return time $\tau$ is a $C^1$ function on the domain, not a constant;
the reference crossing time $t_0$ is only one value of it. (c) Neither map is
asserted to be defined on all of phase space, and no statement here asserts
that a fixed point, a periodic orbit or a return exists for any particular
model. (d) Periods and return times are measured in the frame time
$[t]=\tau$ ([[def-cm01-units]]); a return time must be positive for the
periodicity reading of clause (iii) to apply.
items.strategy: A vocabulary item: the stroboscopic map with its recursive forward domain, the autonomous special case, and the local Poincare return map with its C1 diffeomorphism property supplied by the first-return theorem.
items.physical_scope: The two maps used to reduce the model's dynamics to discrete time: the stroboscopic map at the period of a P-periodic force model, defined only on states whose motion exists over the full period, with iterates recursively defined and fixed points in bijection with P-periodic motions; and the local Poincare return map of a transversal section of an autonomous model, whose existence, C1 regularity and local invertibility are supplied from the first-return mapping theorem. The item asserts no completeness, no global return and no all-time existence of iterates.

items.title: Chaos in the stated sense for maps of the model: topological mixing, dense periodic points and sensitive dependence, as one precise list among several
items.statement:
Let $(X,d)$ be a nonempty metric space ([[def-metric-space]]) and let
$f:X\to X$ be a map. Say that $f$ is **chaotic in the stated sense** when all
four of the following hold; this is the definition of
[[def-cm-topologically-mixing-dense-periodic-and-sensitive-maps]], quoted here
to fix the exact content used on this page:

1. $f$ is **continuous** with respect to the metric topology
   ([[def-metric-continuity]]);
2. $f$ is **topologically mixing**: for all nonempty open sets $U,V\subseteq X$
   there is an integer $N$ with $f^n(U)\cap V\ne\emptyset$ for every $n\ge N$;
3. the periodic points of $f$ are **dense** in $X$: every nonempty open subset
   of $X$ meets $\{x\in X:f^n(x)=x\text{ for some }n\ge1\}$
   ([[def-dense-top]]);
4. $f$ has **sensitive dependence on initial conditions**: there is
   $\delta>0$ (a sensitivity constant) such that for every $x\in X$ and every
   $\varepsilon>0$ there are $y\in X$ and $n\ge1$ with $d(x,y)<\varepsilon$
   and $d(f^n(x),f^n(y))\ge\delta$.

The predicate is applied on this page only to maps of the model: the
stroboscopic map $\Psi$ of a periodic model, restricted to a subset
$X\subseteq\Sigma$ with $\Psi(X)\subseteq X$, or the local return map $P$ of a
transversal section restricted to an invariant subset of its domain
([[def-cm16-stroboscopic-and-poincare-maps]] clauses (i) and (iii)), with $d$
the Euclidean distance of the state chart restricted to $X$. The properties
are relative to that set and that metric; changing the invariant set or
rescaling coordinates changes the property list in general.

**Conventions and scope.** (a) This is one precise list among several
inequivalent usages of the word "chaos" in the literature; the page asserts
none of the other usages, and no item of the page claims that a model is
"chaotic" without exhibiting the four properties for a stated map, set and
metric. (b) The four properties are independent: the identity map of a
nonempty space has dense periodic points and is not mixing whenever the space
has more than one point; a hyperbolic equilibrium can have positive
finite-time growth rates while its compact invariant sets are single points
(see the page's counterexample on the repulsive linear model). (c) The list is
purely topological: it asserts no invariant measure, no positivity of an
entropy, no fractal dimension, no statistical stability and no property of any
physical system. (d) A numerical trajectory, a histogram or a plotted section
is not evidence that the four properties hold; they are established by proof
for a stated model.
items.strategy: A vocabulary item fixing one precise chaos list for the model maps (continuity, mixing, dense periodic points, sensitivity) with the independence, topological and non-numerical caveats.
items.physical_scope: The chaos vocabulary of the page, applied to the stroboscopic and Poincare return maps of the declared models: a continuous map of a metric space is chaotic in the stated sense when it is topologically mixing, has dense periodic points and has sensitive dependence on initial conditions with a positive constant, with the three predicates spelled out exactly. The item fixes one precise list among several used in the literature, requires an invariant set and a metric relative to which the properties are stated, and asserts no measure-theoretic property, no entropy or dimension and no empirical claim.

references.title: Gerald Sussman and Jack Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, 2nd ed., §4.3 and §7.4: sensitivity, mixing and the explicit warning that plots and numerical portraits are not proofs of chaos

Iain Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309, Fall 2014), Chapter 7 pp. 143-195: the requirement of a chosen precise definition of chaos and the distinctness of sensitivity, mixing and positive exponents

Konstantin Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Chapter 9 'Chaos': qualitative chaos discussion retained here only as motivation for the precise list

items.title: Hyperbolic linearisation of an equilibrium of the model: exponential dichotomy of the linearised flow, local exponential asymptotic stability in the stable case, and instability in the saddle case
items.statement:
Let an autonomous stability model be fixed whose force map is of class $C^1$
in the state, with state domain $S_0\subseteq\mathbb R^{6N}$, associated
$C^1$ field $G$ and local flow
$\Phi:\Omega\to S_0$ ([[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clauses
(i)-(ii)); all differentiability is that of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Let $z_*\in S_0$ be an
equilibrium state, $G(z_*)=0$, and let
$A:=DG(z_*)$ ([[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]]). Then:

1. **(Exponential dichotomy.)** If no complex eigenvalue of $A$
   ([[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]) has real part
   $0$ --- that is, if $z_*$ is hyperbolic in the sense of
   [[def-cm16-stability-and-hyperbolicity-concepts]] clause (iv) --- then
   there are $A$-invariant subspaces $E_s,E_u\subseteq\mathbb R^{6N}$ with
   $\mathbb R^{6N}=E_s\oplus E_u$ and real constants $C\ge1$, $c>0$ such
   that, with the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the
   exponential series $e^{tA}$:
   $$\lVert e^{tA}v\rVert_2\le Ce^{-ct}\lVert v\rVert_2\ (v\in E_s,\ t\ge0), \qquad \lVert e^{tA}v\rVert_2\ge C^{-1}e^{ct}\lVert v\rVert_2\ (v\in E_u,\ t\ge0),$$
   $$\lVert e^{tA}v\rVert_2\le Ce^{ct}\lVert v\rVert_2\ (v\in E_u,\ t\le0),$$
   and $E_s=\{v:e^{tA}v\to0\ (t\to+\infty)\}$,
   $E_u=\{v:e^{tA}v\to0\ (t\to-\infty)\}$. The spaces $E_s,E_u$ are the
   **stable and unstable subspaces** of the linearised flow.
2. **(Stable case.)** If every complex eigenvalue of $A$ has negative real
   part, then $z_*$ is locally exponentially asymptotically stable: there are
   $\delta>0$, $\beta\ge1$, $\gamma>0$ such that every maximal solution $z$
   of the model with $\lVert z(0)-z_*\rVert_2<\delta$ is defined for all
   $t\ge0$ and satisfies
   $$\lVert z(t)-z_*\rVert_2\le\beta e^{-\gamma t}\lVert z(0)-z_*\rVert_2\qquad(t\ge0).$$
   In particular $z_*$ is Lyapunov stable and asymptotically stable
   ([[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]]).
3. **(Saddle case.)** If no complex eigenvalue of $A$ has real part $0$ and
   at least one has positive real part, then $z_*$ is unstable: there is
   $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that for every $\delta>0$ there are a state $z_0$
   with $\lVert z_0-z_*\rVert_2<\delta$ and a time $t_1>0$ such that the
   maximal solution through $z_0$ is defined on $[0,t_1]$ and
   $\lVert z(t_1)-z_*\rVert_2=\varepsilon_0$.
4. **(Rates, charts and scope.)** The constants $C,c,\beta,\gamma$ and the
   subspaces depend on $A$ and on the chart scale; the rates $c,\gamma$ have
   dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and the chart dependence of the eigenvalues is that
   recorded in [[def-cm16-stability-and-hyperbolicity-concepts]] clause
   (vi)(b). No conclusion is asserted when some eigenvalue has zero real part
   (the centre case), and no statement is made about the size of the stable
   set, the basin of attraction, uniformity in a family of models or any
   empirical realization.
items.strategy: Direct transfer of the exponential dichotomy, Lyapunov stability and instability suppliers to an equilibrium of the model field, with the chart and centre-case qualifications.
items.physical_scope: The consequences of the hyperbolic linearisation of an equilibrium state of an autonomous model whose force map is of class C1 in the state: invariant stable and unstable subspaces of the linearised flow with exponential estimates and exponential separation from the equilibrium; local exponential asymptotic stability of the equilibrium when the whole spectrum lies in the open left half-plane; and instability when no eigenvalue lies on the imaginary axis and one lies in the open right half-plane. The rates and constants belong to the linearised flow in the declared state chart; no centre-case, global, parameter-uniform or empirical statement is made.

references.title: Iain Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309, Fall 2014), §7.3 pp. 164-172 with the corrected epsilon-delta definitions: linearisation at an equilibrium, stability in the stable case and instability from a positive real eigenvalue

Konstantin Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), §§3.2, 5.6: the source's linearised-stability discussion with its omitted hypotheses, replaced here by the complete supplier statements

Gerald Sussman and Jack Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, 2nd ed., §4.3: stable and unstable sets and the warning that the exponential dichotomy must be proved rather than read off a picture

items.title: The two-rotor model: a positive-measure family of invariant Lagrangian tori with Diophantine frequencies for sufficiently small coupling, with the explicit units and the stated scope
items.statement:
Adopt the **two-rotor model**: two ideal rotors with fixed axes, equal moments
of inertia $\mathcal I>0$, angular coordinates $\theta_1,\theta_2$ in
$\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$ (radians, dimensionless), conjugate angular momenta
$\Pi_1,\Pi_2$, the physical Hamiltonian
$$H_{\mathrm{phys}}(\theta,\Pi)=\frac{\Pi_1^2}{2\mathcal I}+\frac{\Pi_2^2}{2\mathcal I} +E_0\varepsilon\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2$$
on the phase domain $(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^2\times\mathbb R^2$, with the
canonical two-form $d\theta_1\wedge d\Pi_1+d\theta_2\wedge d\Pi_2$ and
Hamilton equations $\theta'=\partial_\Pi H_{\mathrm{phys}}$,
$\Pi'=-\partial_\theta H_{\mathrm{phys}}$; here $E_0>0$ is an energy scale
and $\varepsilon\ge0$ a dimensionless coupling. All quantities are model data;
$[H_{\mathrm{phys}}]=\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}$, $[\Pi_i]=\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$,
$[\mathcal I]=\mu\ell^2$ ([[def-cm01-units]]). Put
$$J_0:=\sqrt{\mathcal I E_0},\qquad t_0:=\frac{J_0}{E_0}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathcal I}{E_0}},\qquad \omega_0:=\frac1{t_0}=\sqrt{\frac{E_0}{\mathcal I}},$$
and read the **dimensionless model** through $I_i:=\Pi_i/J_0$ and the
dimensionless time $s:=t/t_0$,
$$H(I,\vartheta)=\tfrac12\bigl(I_1^2+I_2^2\bigr)+\varepsilon\cos\vartheta_1\cos\vartheta_2.$$
Let $C^*:=\{\nu\in\mathbb R^2:\lvert\nu\rvert_\infty\le\tfrac1{16}\}$ be the
declared frequency cube and, for $\tau>1$ and $\alpha>0$, let
$$\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}:=\Bigl\{\nu\in C^*:\lvert k\cdot\nu\rvert\ge\alpha\lvert k\rvert_1^{-\tau} \ \text{for all }k\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{0\}\Bigr\}$$
be its $(\alpha,\tau)$-Diophantine subset
([[def-holomorphic-kam-domain-and-diophantine-labels]]). Then for every
$\tau>1$ there is a constant $c>0$, depending only on the declared
dimensionless data (the action cube, the analyticity strip, the exponent
$\tau$ and the bounds $M_2=2$ and $\lvert F\rvert\le\varepsilon$ below), such
that for every $0<\alpha<c$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ with
$\varepsilon\le c\,\alpha^2$:

1. **(Positive measure of frequencies.)** The Diophantine set has positive
   Lebesgue measure, with
   $$\lvert\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}\rvert\ge\lvert C^*\rvert-C_{2,\tau}\, (\operatorname{diam}C^*)\,\alpha=\frac1{64}-\frac{C_{2,\tau}}{8}\,\alpha,$$
   where $C_{2,\tau}$ is the lattice constant of
   [[lem-diophantine-resonance-slab-measure]].
2. **(Invariant Lagrangian tori.)** For every $\nu\in\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$
   there is a continuous injective map
   $\widehat\Psi_\nu:\mathbb T^2\to(\mathbb R^2)\times\mathbb T^2$ that is a
   homeomorphism onto its image, is Lagrangian
   ($\widehat\Psi_\nu^*\omega=0$ for the two-form $\omega$ of the
   dimensionless model), and satisfies
   $$X_H\bigl(\widehat\Psi_\nu(\vartheta)\bigr)=\sum_{j=1}^2\nu_j\, \partial_{\vartheta_j}\widehat\Psi_\nu(\vartheta);$$
   consequently the model's motions on the torus are, in the lifted angles,
   $\vartheta(s)=\vartheta(0)+\nu s$, and the physical angles evolve as
   $\theta(t)=\theta(0)+\omega_0\,\nu\,t$: the torus carries quasi-periodic
   motion with angular frequencies $\omega_0\nu_1,\omega_0\nu_2$. The
   parametrisation is close to the unperturbed one and Lipschitz in $\nu$ with
   the bounds of [[thm-positive-measure-analytic-kam-family]] clause 3.
3. **(Scope.)** Nothing is asserted about the complement of
   $\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$ (resonant or non-Diophantine labels), about tori
   surviving outside the smallness threshold, about all initial data, about
   diffusive or chaotic behaviour of the complement, or about any laboratory
   rotor: the smallness condition $\varepsilon\le c\alpha^2$ is a model-data
   condition, the constant $c$ is not computed numerically here, and no
   measured value of $\mathcal I$, $E_0$ or $\varepsilon$ is used or implied.
items.strategy: Verification of the analytic KAM hypotheses for the declared two-rotor potential and unit restoration, concluding positive-measure Diophantine tori and quasi-periodic motions with angular frequencies omega0 nu.
items.physical_scope: The conditional KAM statement for the adopted two-rotor model: two ideal fixed-axis rotors of equal positive moment of inertia with the smooth interaction potential E0 epsilon cos theta1 cos theta2. For every Diophantine exponent tau>1 there is a constant c>0 determined by the declared dimensionless data such that for 0<alpha<c and 0<epsilon<=c alpha^2 the set of frequencies satisfying the Diophantine bound has positive Lebesgue measure in the declared action cube, and for every such frequency the model has an invariant Lagrangian torus whose motions are quasi-periodic with angular frequencies nu_i/t0. The item asserts nothing about the complement of that frequency set (resonant or non-Diophantine labels), nothing about all initial data, no chaos or diffusion statement, no measured value of any parameter and no empirical realization; epsilon<=c alpha^2 is a model-data smallness condition.

Rafael de la Llave, A Tutorial on KAM Theory (expanded version of the Seattle 1999 lectures; complete text), §3.3 pp. 32-36 and §6.1 pp. 92-100: Diophantine sets and the measure of the resonant slabs

Gerald Sussman and Jack Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, 2nd ed., §4.6: the explicit statement that SICM does not prove KAM and the requirement of regularity, twist and smallness hypotheses

items.title: A smooth periodically forced one-coordinate model with a transverse homoclinic horseshoe: the physical stroboscopic map has a compact invariant set conjugate to the shift, chaotic in the stated sense
items.statement:
Grant the Axioms of Countable and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]), inherited from the
supplier theorem below.

**(i) The model.** Fix a length scale $\ell_0>0$, a mass $m>0$, a frequency
scale $\omega_0>0$, a dimensionless amplitude $a\ge100$, and a pulse width
$\delta>0$. Let $w$ be the normalized smooth bump and $\beta_\delta$ the
smooth $P$-periodic pulse of [[def-smooth-periodic-oscillator-pulse-model]]
with $P:=\pi/2+\delta$, $\beta_\delta=0$ on $[0,\pi/2]$ and
$\beta_\delta(t)=\delta^{-1}w((t-\pi/2)/\delta)$ on $[\pi/2,P]$. The
**physical pulsed oscillator model** is the one-label model on the
configuration domain $Q:=\mathbb R$ with fixed mass $m$ and the
$T_p$-periodic force map
$$F(T,Q):=-m\omega_0^2\Bigl[Q+\ell_0\,\beta_\delta(\omega_0T)\Bigl(a-\frac{Q^2}{\ell_0^2}\Bigr)\Bigr], \qquad T_p:=\frac{P}{\omega_0},$$
that is, a model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with
$m\ddot Q=F(T,Q)$ and $F(T+T_p,Q)=F(T,Q)$; its motions are the $C^2$ curves of
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]. Its canonical momentum is
$\Pi=m\dot Q$ and its stroboscopic map at period $T_p$ is the map $\Psi_\delta$
of [[def-cm16-stroboscopic-and-poincare-maps]] clause (i).

**(ii) The horseshoe.** There is $\delta_0>0$, depending only on $a$ and the
bump $w$, such that for every $0<\delta<\delta_0$ there is a homeomorphism
$H_\delta$ of the two-sign shift space $(X_\pm,D_\pm)$ of
[[def-bilateral-symbol-and-bounded-sequence-space]] onto a compact subset
$\Lambda_\delta^{\mathrm{phys}}$ of the physical phase plane such that
$$\Psi_\delta\circ H_\delta=H_\delta\circ S_\pm,$$
so that $\Lambda_\delta^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is compact and $\Psi_\delta$-invariant
and the restriction $\Psi_\delta|_{\Lambda_\delta^{\mathrm{phys}}}$ is
conjugate to the shift; with the Euclidean metric of the chart this
restriction is chaotic in the stated sense of
[[def-cm16-chaos-list-for-model-maps]]: continuous, topologically mixing, dense
periodic points and sensitive dependence with a positive constant.

**(iii) Hyperbolic points and transverse homoclinic orbits.** The two constant
codes give two hyperbolic fixed points of $\Psi_\delta$, one of each sign; and
for every code $\sigma\in X_\pm$ that is constant outside a finite set, the
point $H_\delta(\sigma)$ is a transverse homoclinic point of the corresponding
fixed point, in the sense of the stable and unstable cones and line fields of
[[def-stable-unstable-cones-and-line-slopes]]; distinct such codes give
distinct points.

**(iv) Explicit bounds.** Write $R:=\sqrt a+3$. Every state in
$\Lambda_\delta^{\mathrm{phys}}$ satisfies
$$\lvert Q\rvert\le R\,\ell_0,\qquad \lvert\Pi\rvert=m\ell_0\omega_0\,\lvert p\rvert\le m\ell_0\omega_0R,$$
and every coded trajectory exists for all times and remains in that box at the
stroboscopic times. For $a=100$ the bounds are $\lvert Q\rvert\le13\,\ell_0$
and $\lvert\Pi\rvert\le13\,m\ell_0\omega_0$.

**(v) Scope.** The forcing is an adopted phenomenological polynomial pulse
generated by the explicit bump; it is not claimed to be an observed drive or
apparatus, and no measurement, calibration or uncertainty is involved. The
result is about this one model: it does not assert chaos for every driven
pendulum, for separatrix splitting in gravitational or vortex models, for
Hénon-Heiles energies, or for any numerical portrait, and it does not
validate a first-order Melnikov calculation by analogy
([[def-cm16-chaos-list-for-model-maps]] clause (d)).
items.strategy: Model construction and scaling transfer: the smooth pulsed one-coordinate Newtonian model is a force model of the framework, and the supplier conjugacy transports to its physical stroboscopic map with explicit coded-state bounds.
items.physical_scope: The conditional chaos theorem for one declared smooth mechanical model: a single label of fixed positive mass on a line, subject to the harmonic restoring force plus a smooth P-periodic polynomial pulse forcing derived from an explicit bump function. For every pulse width below a threshold depending only on the dimensionless amplitude parameter a>=100 and the bump, the physical stroboscopic map of the model has a compact invariant set on which it is conjugate to the two-sign shift, is topologically mixing, has dense periodic points and sensitive dependence, with two hyperbolic fixed points and transverse homoclinic points, and all coded states satisfy the explicit bounds |Q|<=sqrt(a+3) l0 and |Pi|<=m l0 w0 sqrt(a+3). The model is an adopted mechanical model, not a reported apparatus; no measurement, no empirical chaos claim and no claim about other driven or nearly integrable models is made.

items.title: Poincare recurrence for the model's Hamiltonian flow on a bounded invariant set of finite phase volume: almost every state of any Borel subset returns to it infinitely often
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), inherited from the phase-volume preservation
theorem [[pthm-cm13-liouville]] (its measure-preservation clause uses the
change-of-variables theorem under that assumption). Adopt the force model with
potential presentation and the Hamiltonian data of [[pthm-cm13-liouville]]:
time-independent potential $U:Q\to\mathbb R$ with residual forces
$d\equiv0$, Cartesian phase domain $W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
([[def-cm13-two-form]]), Hamiltonian
$$H:I_0\times W\to\mathbb R,\qquad H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(x),$$
phase-volume form $\Omega=\omega^{\wedge3N}/(3N)!$, and local flow
$\Phi_t=\Phi(t,\cdot)$ on the neighbourhood $U_0$ of
[[pthm-cm13-flow-preservation]]. Let $A\subseteq U_0$ be a bounded Borel set
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]) with $\overline A\subseteq U_0$, and suppose
that the flow is defined on $A$ for all real times and maps $A$ onto itself:
$$\Phi_t(A)=A\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
so that $A$ is invariant in the sense of
[[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clause (iv). Then
$\lambda_{6N}(A)<\infty$, and for every Borel set $E\subseteq A$ almost every
$x\in E$ with respect to the Lebesgue measure $\lambda_{6N}$ of the chart
([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]) has
$$\Phi_n(x)\in E\qquad\text{for infinitely many }n\ge1.$$
The time unit is the frame time $[t]=\tau$ ([[def-cm01-units]]), so
"infinitely many $n$" means infinitely many returns at unit time steps.
items.strategy: Composition of the phase-volume preservation theorem with the finite-measure recurrence theorem: a bounded invariant Borel set of finite phase volume has almost-everywhere infinite returns at unit time steps, under countable choice.
items.physical_scope: Poincare recurrence for the Hamiltonian flow of a declared autonomous potential presentation: if a bounded Borel set of phase space with finite Lebesgue measure is invariant under the flow (as happens for the compact energy sublevel sets of a trapped one-dimensional model), then for every Borel subset of it almost every state returns to that subset infinitely often at integer multiples of the time unit. The statement assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice, inherited from the phase-volume preservation theorem, and it asserts nothing about return times, about which states return, about infinite phase volume or incomplete flows, and nothing empirical.

items.title: Scope of the stability, perturbation and chaos statements: conditional model deductions, the limits of finite-time and numerical evidence, and the empirical qualifications
items.statement:
This remark records what the page's statements do and do not establish. It adds
no new claim of its own.

**1. Model deductions only.** Every theorem of the page is a conditional
deduction about the declared model class of
[[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]]: a force model with stated
masses, configuration domain, regularity and — where relevant — periodicity.
The conclusions about equilibria, tori, horseshoes and recurrence are
properties of those models. None of them asserts that a physical system is
exactly such a model, and none carries a measured value: the constants
appearing in the statements (couplings, energy scales, pulse parameters, the
smallness thresholds $c$ and $\delta_0$) are model data, and no measurement,
calibration, sampling or uncertainty budget occurs anywhere on the page.

**2. Stability is not attraction, and one notion is not another.**
[[pthm-cm16-energy-stability-and-instability]] establishes Lyapunov stability
of a strict minimum, linear instability from a negative Hessian eigenvalue,
nonlinear instability from a strictly concave potential, and the absence of
asymptotic stability under exact energy conservation. The degenerate case (a
zero Hessian eigenvalue) and the mixed saddle case (a negative eigenvalue
together with oscillatory directions) are deliberately left open: only the
linear statement is made there. The harmonic-oscillator counterexample shows
that the page's stability vocabulary cannot be collapsed.

**3. Linearisation is finite-time and local.**
[[pthm-cm16-variational-equation-and-linearization]] and
[[pthm-cm16-hyperbolic-linearization]] are finite-time statements on declared
balls with declared quantitative bounds. A finite-time growth rate computed
from them is a number attached to a state, a tangent vector and an interval
([[def-cm16-finite-time-growth-rates]]); a positive rate is not a definition
of chaos, and a positive real eigenvalue of a linearisation proves instability
of the equilibrium, not chaos of the flow. Eigenvalues and rates are
chart-dependent unless the state coordinates are scaled with fixed factors.

**4. Chaos is a proved property of a stated map and set.**
[[pthm-cm16-separatrix-splitting-and-horseshoe]] proves the four properties of
[[def-cm16-chaos-list-for-model-maps]] for the stroboscopic map of one smooth
periodically pulsed oscillator, restricted to an explicitly constructed
compact invariant set, by transferring the supplied conjugacy to the shift
through a linear scaling. It is existence for that model under its small-pulse
condition; it is not a claim about all driven oscillators, about every
separatrix, about Hénon-Heiles energies or about any numerical portrait.
Quantified numerical trajectories and plotted sections are computations under
chosen parameters; they are neither experiments nor proofs. The page contains
no experiment item and reports no observed data.

**5. KAM persistence is a positive-measure conditional statement.**
[[pthm-cm16-two-rotor-kam]] gives, for the adopted two-rotor potential and
sufficiently small coupling, a positive-measure set of Diophantine frequencies
whose tori persist, with quasi-periodic motions on them and explicit unit
restoration. It says nothing about the complement of that set, about resonant
gaps, about all initial data, about chaotic diffusion, or about a laboratory
rotor. The threshold $\varepsilon\le c\alpha^2$ is a model-data condition; the
constant $c$ is not computed numerically and no empirical smallness is
asserted.

**6. Recurrence needs finite volume and invariance.**
[[pthm-cm16-recurrence-for-finite-volume-models]] assumes a bounded
flow-invariant Borel set of finite phase volume; its conclusion is
almost-everywhere with respect to phase volume and gives no return time, no
rate and no individual-state statement. Free and unconfined models fail the
hypothesis, and the theorem says nothing about them or about thermodynamic
irreversibility.

**7. Choice conventions.** The horseshoe theorem assumes the Axioms of
Countable and Dependent Choice, inherited from its supplier, and the
recurrence theorem assumes Countable Choice, inherited from
[[pthm-cm13-liouville]]. All other statements of the page are choice-free:
their suppliers use finite-dimensional linear algebra, explicit
constructions and finite estimates. No item reaches a recorded or unproved
set-theoretic item.

**8. Relation to the sources.** The four complete works consulted for this
page (Tong, Likharev, SICM and Stewart) supply the model formulations,
worked examples and caveats; their informal stability and chaos discussions
are replaced by the exact supplier statements, and their numerical portraits
are treated as illustrations, never as evidence. The empirical status of any
model on this page would require a separately specified apparatus, sampling
model and statistical analysis, which this page does not provide.

The remark makes no new mathematical or empirical claim.

items.title: The ideal pendulum on declared data: strict minimum and Lyapunov stability at the downward equilibrium, negative Hessian and instability at the upward equilibrium, the exact linearisation frequencies, and failure of attraction
items.statement:
**Declared model data.** Take one label on the real line as the angle chart of
the ideal planar pendulum: the chart domain is $\Omega:=\mathbb R$, the
configuration coordinate is the angle $q$ (radians, identified modulo $2\pi$
at the end), the kinetic metric is the constant matrix
$M:=m\ell^2$ with $m:=1\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\ell:=1\ \mathrm m$, and the potential
is
$$U(q):=mg\ell\,(1-\cos q),\qquad g:=9.81\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}},\qquad mg\ell=9.81\ \mathrm J .$$
This is the mechanical chart datum of
[[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]] with
$\Omega=\mathbb R$, $M$ constant and $U$ of class $C^\infty$. Its equations
are $m\ell^2\ddot q=-mg\ell\sin q$, equivalently
$\ddot q=-(g/\ell)\sin q$.

**Assertions to check.** (i) $q=0$ and $q=\pi$ are mechanical equilibria;
(ii) at $q=0$ the potential is a strict local minimum and
[[pthm-cm16-energy-stability-and-instability]] clause 1 makes $(0,0)$
Lyapunov stable, while the linearised frequencies are
$\pm i\sqrt{g/\ell}=\pm i\,3\sqrt{109}/10\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and the
equilibrium is not asymptotically stable; (iii) at $q=\pi$ the Hessian is
$-mg\ell<0$ and clause 3 makes $(\pi,0)$ unstable, with linearised rates
$\pm 3\sqrt{109}/10\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.
items.strategy: Declared-data check of the energy-stability theorem on the ideal pendulum: strict minimum and stability with imaginary frequencies; negative Hessian and instability with real rates; failure of attraction.
items.physical_scope: A declared-data check of the page's energy-stability theorem on the ideal planar pendulum: with mass 1 kg, length 1 m and g=9.81 m s^-2 in the angle chart, the downward equilibrium is a strict minimum, hence Lyapunov stable but not attracting, with purely imaginary linearisation frequencies; the upward equilibrium has a strictly negative Hessian, hence is unstable, with the real linearisation rates. All data are declared model data; no measurement and no empirical comparison is made.

items.title: Two declared linear models worked through: the harmonic flow has zero finite-time growth in every direction, while the repulsive linear model has exact rates $\pm1$ and the positive Lyapunov exponent $1$ at its equilibrium
items.statement:
**Declared model data.** Work in the one-dimensional chart $\Omega:=\mathbb R$
with the constant kinetic metric $M:=1$ (dimensionless units). Two potentials
are declared:

1. the **harmonic model** $U_1(q):=\tfrac12q^2$, with field
   $G_1(q,v)=(v,-q)$ and motion map
   $\Phi_t^1(q_0,v_0)=(q_0\cos t+v_0\sin t,\,-q_0\sin t+v_0\cos t)$;
2. the **repulsive linear model** $U_2(q):=-\tfrac12q^2$, with field
   $G_2(q,v)=(v,q)$ and motion map
   $\Phi_t^2(q_0,v_0)=\bigl(\tfrac12(q_0+v_0)e^{t}+\tfrac12(q_0-v_0)e^{-t},\,
   \tfrac12(q_0+v_0)e^{t}-\tfrac12(q_0-v_0)e^{-t}\bigr)$.

**Assertions to check.** (i) Both displayed maps are the local flows of their
fields; (ii) for the harmonic model
$D_{a}\Phi_t^1(a)$ is the rotation
$\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$, so every
finite-time tangent growth rate vanishes and every existing Lyapunov exponent
is $0$; (iii) for the repulsive model the rates along the directions
$(1,-1)$ and $(1,1)$ are $-1$ and $+1$, so the Lyapunov exponent of the
equilibrium along the unstable eigenvector is $1$.
items.strategy: Declared-data check of the variational equation and the growth-rate definition on two linear models: zero rates for the harmonic flow, exact rates plus and minus one for the repulsive flow.
items.physical_scope: A declared-data check of the page's finite-time growth definition and of the variational-equation supplier on two dimensionless linear mechanical models: the harmonic model M=K=1 has the rotation flow, whose derivative is orthogonal, so every finite-time tangent growth rate vanishes identically and every Lyapunov exponent that exists is zero; the repulsive linear model U=-q^2/2 has the hyperbolic flow, with exact rates +1 and -1 along the eigenvectors of the linearisation and Lyapunov exponent 1 at the equilibrium along the unstable direction. The check is model-data substitution, not a measurement and not a statement about chaotic behaviour.

items.title: The planar isotropic oscillator: the stroboscopic map at half period is minus the identity, every state is periodic, the periodic points are dense, and the map is neither mixing nor sensitive
items.statement:
**Declared model data.** Take two dimensionless labels in the plane, with
configuration domain $\Omega:=\mathbb R^2$, constant kinetic metric
$M:=I_2$ and potential $U(q):=\tfrac12\lVert q\rVert_2^2$ in the cartesian
chart $(x,y)$ of [[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]].
The field is
$$G(x,y,v_x,v_y)=(v_x,v_y,-x,-y),$$
and the motion through $(x_0,y_0,v_{x0},v_{y0})$ is
$$x(t)=x_0\cos t+v_{x0}\sin t,\qquad v_x(t)=-x_0\sin t+v_{x0}\cos t,$$
and likewise in the $y$ coordinate. Consider the stroboscopic map $\Psi_P$ of
[[def-cm16-stroboscopic-and-poincare-maps]] clause (ii) for this autonomous
model, and the section $\Sigma_+:=\{y=0,\ v_y>0\}$ with its first-return map.

**Assertions to check.** (i) The displayed curves are the model's motions;
(ii) $\Psi_\pi=-\mathrm{id}$ and $\Psi_{2\pi}=\mathrm{id}$, so every state of
the model is periodic under the flow with period $2\pi$ and every point is a
periodic point of $\Psi_\pi$ with period dividing $2$; (iii) the first-return
map of $\Sigma_+$ is the identity; (iv) with the Euclidean metric of the
phase chart, $\Psi_\pi$ on $X:=\mathbb R^4$ is continuous and has dense
periodic points, but is not topologically mixing and has no sensitivity
constant, hence is not chaotic in the stated sense of
[[def-cm16-chaos-list-for-model-maps]].
items.strategy: Declared-data check of the discrete-time vocabulary: the half-period stroboscopic map is minus the identity, so periodic points are dense but mixing and sensitivity fail.
items.physical_scope: A declared-data check of the page's discrete-time vocabulary on the planar isotropic oscillator with unit mass and unit stiffness: the flow is an explicit rotation of each coordinate plane, the stroboscopic map at period pi is minus the identity, at period 2pi it is the identity, the Poincare first-return map to the section y=0, vy>0 is the identity, every state is periodic, periodic points are dense in the phase plane, and the map fails topological mixing and sensitivity, so it is not chaotic in the stated sense. The check is model-data substitution; it reports no measurement.

items.title: The pulsed horseshoe on declared data: $a=100$, the radicand box $[74,126]$, the contraction factor $1/\sqrt{74}$, the fixed points $1\pm\sqrt{101}$, and the physical bounds of the coded states at $\ell_0=1\,\mathrm m$, $m=1\,\mathrm{kg}$, $\omega_0=2\pi\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$
items.statement:
**Declared model data.** Take the physical pulsed oscillator of
[[pthm-cm16-separatrix-splitting-and-horseshoe]] clause (i) with
$$a:=100,\qquad \ell_0:=1\ \mathrm m,\qquad m:=1\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad \omega_0:=2\pi\ \mathrm{s^{-1}},$$
and a pulse width $0<\delta<\delta_0$ with $\delta_0$ the supplier threshold
(not evaluated numerically here). Let $R:=\sqrt a+3$, $L:=\sqrt{a-2R}$ and let
$r_\pm$ be the fixed points of the limiting quadratic map.

**Assertions to check.** (i) $R=13$ and the coding radicands
$a+x_{n-1}+x_{n+1}$ lie in $[74,126]=[a-2R,a+2R]$, with
$\sqrt{126}<13=R$; (ii) the contraction factor of the coding map is
$1/L=1/\sqrt{74}$ and $r_\pm=1\pm\sqrt{101}$; (iii) for the limiting pulse,
$K\circ R_0=F$ with $R_0(q,p)=(p,-q)$, $K(q,p)=(q,p+q^2-a)$ and
$F(x,y)=(y,y^2-a-x)$; (iv) every coded state satisfies
$\lvert Q\rvert\le13\ \mathrm m$ and $\lvert\Pi\rvert\le26\pi\
\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and the forcing period is
$T_p=(\pi/2+\delta)/(2\pi)\ \mathrm s$.
items.strategy: Declared-data evaluation of the pulsed-horseshoe constants at a=100: coding box, radicand interval, contraction factor, fixed points, kick composition and physical bounds.
items.physical_scope: A declared-data check of the constants and bounds in the page's pulsed-horseshoe theorem: at amplitude a=100 the coding box is R=13, the radicands lie in [74,126], the contraction factor is 1/sqrt(74), the fixed points are 1 plus or minus sqrt(101), the limiting kick satisfies K composed with the rotation = F, and with length scale 1 m, mass 1 kg and frequency scale 2 pi per second the coded states are bounded by 13 m in position and 26 pi kg m per second in momentum, with period (pi/2+delta)/(2 pi) seconds. All quantities are declared model data; the pulse-width threshold is not numerically evaluated and no measurement is involved.

items.title: A positive Lyapunov exponent at a hyperbolic equilibrium does not produce a chaotic invariant set: the repulsive linear model has rate $1$ at its equilibrium and no compact invariant set with more than one point
items.statement:
**False statement.** *If an autonomous stability model has an equilibrium whose
linearisation possesses an eigenvalue with positive real part and the model's
flow has the positive Lyapunov exponent equal to that eigenvalue at the
equilibrium along an unstable direction, then the model's flow possesses a
compact invariant set that is chaotic in the stated sense of
[[def-cm16-chaos-list-for-model-maps]] (continuous, topologically mixing, dense
periodic points, sensitive dependence).*
items.strategy: Counterexample by classification of compact invariant sets: the repulsive linear model has a positive exponent at its equilibrium yet every compact invariant set is a single point that fails sensitivity.
items.physical_scope: A declared-model counterexample refuting the implication from a positive Lyapunov exponent at an equilibrium to the existence of a chaotic compact invariant set: the dimensionless repulsive linear model U(q)=-q^2/2 has the positive exponent 1 at its equilibrium along the unstable direction, its equilibrium is nonlinearly unstable, and yet every compact invariant set of its flow is the single point {0}, which fails the sensitivity clause of the page's chaos list. The counterexample is a model computation; it reports no measurement.

items.strategy: Counterexample on the harmonic model: the equilibrium is Lyapunov stable while every nonzero datum keeps its distance, in agreement with the no-attraction clause of the energy theorem.

items.title: A trapped one-label model: the compact energy sublevel of the radial quartic potential is invariant with finite phase volume, so the recurrence theorem applies, while the free model's energy sublevels are unbounded and the hypothesis fails
items.statement:
**Declared model data.** Take one label in the flat Cartesian presentation of
[[pthm-cm16-recurrence-for-finite-volume-models]] with $N=1$: the configuration
domain is $Q:=\mathbb R^3$, the mass is $m:=1$ so that $\mathsf M=I_3$ and
$W=Q\times\mathbb R^3$ with coordinates $(x,v)$, and the **radial quartic
potential** is
$$U(x):=\tfrac14\lVert x\rVert_2^4,$$
a $C^\infty$ datum of [[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]]
with field $G(x,v)=(v,-\lVert x\rVert_2^2x)$ and energy
$E(x,v)=\tfrac12\lVert v\rVert_2^2+\tfrac14\lVert x\rVert_2^4$. For $E_1>0$ put
$$A_{E_1}:=\{(x,v)\in W:E(x,v)\le E_1\}.$$

**Assertions to check.** (i) $A_{E_1}$ is a nonempty compact Borel subset of
$W$ with
$\lambda_6(A_{E_1})\le\bigl(2(4E_1)^{1/4}\bigr)^3\bigl(2\sqrt{2E_1}\bigr)^3=512\,E_1^{9/4}<\infty$;
(ii) the flow of the model maps $A_{E_1}$ onto itself for every real time, so
the hypotheses of [[pthm-cm16-recurrence-for-finite-volume-models]] are met
and for every Borel $E\subseteq A_{E_1}$ almost every state of $E$ returns to
$E$ infinitely often; (iii) for the flat model $U\equiv0$ the energy sublevels
are unbounded, the phase measure of $W$ is infinite, and the
nonzero-velocity free motion leaves every bounded set, so the finite-volume
hypothesis is not automatic.
items.strategy: Declared-data realization of the recurrence hypotheses on the trapped quartic model and the failure of the finite-volume hypothesis for the free model.
items.physical_scope: A declared-data check of the page's recurrence theorem on a trapped one-dimensional model: for the unit-mass quartic potential U(q)=q^4/4 the energy sublevel {E<=E1}, E1>0, is compact with finite area bounded by 4(4E1)^{1/4}sqrt(2E1), invariant under the flow by energy conservation and compact continuation, so the recurrence theorem gives almost-everywhere infinite returns; in contrast the free model U=0 has unbounded energy sublevels and a nonrecurrent nonzero-velocity motion, showing the finite-volume hypothesis is not automatic. The check uses no measurement.

items.title: Unit restoration and calibration of the two-rotor KAM statement: the scaling identities at $\mathcal I=E_0=1$, the physical angular frequencies, the exclusion of rational frequency labels, and the equal-rescaling invariance
items.statement:
**Declared model data.** Take the two-rotor model of
[[pthm-cm16-two-rotor-kam]] with
$$\mathcal I:=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m^2},\qquad E_0:=1\ \mathrm J,\qquad \varepsilon\ \text{dimensionless},$$
so that $J_0=\sqrt{\mathcal I E_0}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$,
$t_0=J_0/E_0=1\ \mathrm s$ and $\omega_0=\sqrt{E_0/\mathcal I}=1\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.

**Assertions to check.** (i) The dimensions $[H_{\mathrm{phys}}]=\mathrm J$,
$[\Pi_i]=\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$, $[\mathcal I]=\mathrm{kg\,m^2}$,
$[\varepsilon]=1$ and $[\omega_0]=\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]).
(ii) With $I_i=\Pi_i/J_0$, $s=t/t_0$ the physical Hamilton equations
$\dot\theta_i=\Pi_i/\mathcal I$, $\dot\Pi_i=-E_0\varepsilon\sin\theta_i\cos\theta_{3-i}$
are equivalent to $\theta_i'=I_i$,
$I_i'=\varepsilon\sin\vartheta_i\cos\vartheta_{3-i}$.
(iii) A surviving torus with dimensionless label $\nu$ carries the physical
angular frequencies $\omega_0\nu_i$, here $\nu_i\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.
(iv) Every rational label in the cube $C^*$ is excluded from
$\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$ for every $\alpha>0$ and $\tau>1$.
(v) Replacing $(\mathcal I,E_0)$ by $(\lambda\mathcal I,\lambda E_0)$ with
$\lambda>0$ leaves $\omega_0$, the dimensionless model and the smallness
condition unchanged, while rescaling $J_0$ by $\lambda$.
